status_detail: County/EDA search found no verified Madison County, Florida data center project. Madison County Development Council markets industrial/logistics/ag innovation sites, and a county social notice reportedly stated that officials knew of no $1B data center slated for Madison County.
notes: No official application, rezoning, permit, EDA announcement, or local news project record located; beware false-positive Madison County MS/AWS results.

status_detail: Manatee BOCC agenda for July 28, 2026 included multiple commissioner items on data centers and a temporary moratorium for data centers/large-load customers; reporting says commissioners voted unanimously to direct staff toward a moratorium, but no specific project/application was identified.
notes: Coverage indicates regulatory pause, not a named Manatee County data center project.

status_detail: Marion County Legistar file 2026-23648 requested a September 1, 2026 workshop to discuss how to evaluate/manage potential data center applications before receiving one; local coverage also says no data center application was pending.
notes: County is considering rules/moratorium after public opposition, but this is not tied to a submitted project.

status_detail: Silver Fox 606 withdrew its data center/master site plan application on April 29, 2026 after public opposition. Reporting and village-record summaries describe a 2.0-2.2 million square foot data processing/data center proposal at 13820 Silver Fox Road on a 606-acre site.
notes: Applicant tied in reporting to Nelson Ferreira/Ferreira Construction; project apparently withdrawn rather than formally denied.

status_detail: Indiantown Village Council voted unanimously April 30, 2026 to approve a rezoning agreement/master site plan for the 5,722-acre Tesoro Groves PUD; reporting says the PUD was designated for light industrial use and concerns centered on language permitting data-processing/data-center uses.
notes: This is an enabling PUD/land-use approval, not a confirmed standalone data center build; include as broad-mouth potential project because data-processing/data-center use was a core public issue.

project_name: 18300 Southwest Warfield Boulevard data center possibility
status_detail: TCPalm-syndicated reporting noted a separate proposal indicating a data center could be built on 146 acres at 18300 Southwest Warfield Boulevard; developer and application status were not confirmed in accessible reporting.
notes: Low-confidence lead preserved for no-omission; requires follow-up in Indiantown village records.

status_detail: Iron Mountain and Miami-Dade Beacon Council announced a February 26, 2025 groundbreaking for MIA-1, a 150,000 sq ft data center on a 3.4-acre Central Northwest Miami/Westview site, with 16 MW customer IT load and expected opening/completion in 2026.
notes: Official developer and Beacon Council sources; WLRN documents neighborhood concerns and permitting transparency debate.

status_detail: Metrobloks acquired 4.05 acres at 500 NW 137th Avenue, Miami, FL for an AI-ready multi-tenant data center. Its press release cited 15.2 MW; current site page lists MIA A1 as coming soon with 16.8 MW total critical IT and 40.5K sq m whitespace, fully entitled for telecom/data center use.
notes: Capacity field uses current Metrobloks site value; earlier acquisition release reported 15.2 MW.

aliases: RSFG South Dade AI Edge Micro-Datacenter
developer: ReadySetFundGrow LLC / Farrington Capital Group LLC / Remergify
status_detail: ReadySetFundGrow/Remergify announced a planned micro-datacenter, tech incubator, virtual office hub and EV charging hub at 23095 S Dixie Hwy, Homestead; DCD described the Fish Bowl as a proposed glass-enclosed 10-rack micro-data center on a 20,000 sq ft plot, with buildout dependent on financing.
notes: Small edge/micro-datacenter, not hyperscale; capacity not disclosed.

status_detail: Searches of Monroe County, Florida official pages and local/open sources found no commercial data center project, rezoning, tax abatement, or permit record. Hits were unrelated to the county property appraiser 'Online Data Center,' county EOC internal data room, or other states' Monroe County projects.
notes: No verified Florida Keys commercial data center project located; tracker risk page also shows low siting risk rather than a project.

project_name: NextNRG Nassau County data center and microgrid site
status_detail: NextNRG reportedly announced a long-term lease option for an unspecified 1,600-acre Nassau County property: roughly 1,200 acres for a 200 MW smart microgrid and 400 acres 'ideal' for hyperscale data center development. Nassau County and its economic development board said they had no details, applications, rezoning requests, design approvals, or contact from the company.
notes: Preserved as low-confidence announced lead; county official position is no actionable project information/application. Nassau adopted a data-center moratorium and fact-finding process in June 2026.

status_detail: Okaloosa County official-site and local-news searches found no verified data center project, moratorium, rezoning, tax abatement, or building permit. Regional news hits about active data center negotiations were for Escambia County, not Okaloosa; Okaloosa official hits were internal IT/server-room references.
notes: No project found; Facebook/Crestview chatter was not verifiable enough to record as a project.

status_detail: Okeechobee County commissioners effectively killed the Okee-One proposal in April 2026 by dropping proposed 'Special Technology Opportunity Centers' from the long-term growth plan; state support was also pulled. Reporting describes a 200-205 acre campus at the former Okeechobee School for Boys with an initial 9-10 MW data center/training concept.
notes: Capacity stored as 10 MW upper end of reported 9-10 MW initial plan; broader site acreage over 200 acres.

status_detail: HostDime's new seven-story Orlando-area facility in Eatonville/Maitland is under construction/near completion, described by HostDime as 100,000 sq ft at 1 Innovative Pl with Q3 2026 completion; Orlando Economic Partnership's original project page cited an 88,000 sq ft data center and 10 MW of electrical power in Orange County.
notes: Some third-party trackers list 20-30 MW, but official/OEP materials support 10 MW electrical power; developer page emphasizes Q3 2026 completion and 1,000+ racks.

status_detail: HostDime operates a 25,000 sq ft privately owned Tier III edge data center at 440 W. Kennedy Blvd Suite 1, Orlando, with redundant power/network/security and close to 100 Gbps redundant fiber capacity.
notes: Included separately because HostDime says the existing Central Florida data center will operate concurrently with the new Eatonville/Orlando-area facility for near-term demand.
